chapters.title: Historical Introduction
chapters.count_exception: Historical chapter: supplementary exercises are intentionally omitted at the user's direction.

chapters.title: Supersymmetry Algebras
chapters.curation_note: Twelve coherent parents cover the graded algebra, central extensions, positivity and BPS shortening, and the massive and massless representation constructions. Further entries would mainly split single multiplet constructions or repeat state-counting tests.

chapters.title: Supersymmetric Field Theories
chapters.curation_note: Fourteen parents are warranted by the chapter's distinct superspace, component, auxiliary-field, nonlinear-sigma-model, current, and discrete-symmetry arcs. Additional items would mostly isolate intermediate identities from calculations already kept whole.

chapters.title: Supersymmetric Gauge Theories
chapters.curation_note: Thirteen parents span Abelian and non-Abelian field strengths, D-flatness, Higgsing, breaking, holomorphy, and the N=2 extension. More problems would duplicate gauge-component expansions or detach BPS conclusions from their parent derivations.

chapters.title: Supersymmetric Versions of the Standard Model
chapters.curation_note: Fifteen parents reflect the chapter's unusually broad phenomenological scope: unification, flavor and CP, the two-Higgs sector, spectra, gauge mediation, and stable endpoints. Further additions would chiefly vary numerical benchmarks rather than add a new conceptual workflow.

chapters.title: Beyond Perturbation Theory
chapters.curation_note: Fifteen parents preserve complete supersymmetric-quantum-mechanics, gauge-superspace, duality, monodromy, holomorphy, anomaly-matching, and dynamical-breaking analyses. The added Cambridge chiral SU(N)--Spin(8) parent supplies a genuinely distinct Seiberg-duality and anomaly-matching method rather than another split subproblem.

chapters.title: Supergraphs
chapters.curation_note: Ten parents are natural for this short technical chapter: superspace distributions, propagators, D-algebra, non-renormalization, running, and the one-loop effective action each remain intact. A larger count would atomize individual D-algebra steps into artificial standalone exercises.

chapters.title: Supergravity
chapters.curation_note: Twelve parents cover local supersymmetry, gravitino counting and the super-Higgs effect, torsion, the scalar potential, anomaly mediation, gravity mediation, and gravitino phenomenology. Further items would mostly repeat soft-term formulae under alternate hidden-sector assumptions.

chapters.title: Supersymmetry Algebras in Higher Dimensions
chapters.curation_note: Twelve parents give complete arcs for higher-dimensional spinors, maximal multiplets, dimensional reduction, tensorial charges, and brane spectra and dualities. More entries would become a catalogue of dimension-specific decompositions rather than introduce new reasoning.
